That is heart-first rule 6 verbatim, the THIRD instance of that shape already carved there. THE KEYS GO IN THE TEMPLATE OR THEY NEVER COME BACK: v2011 measured exactly this on throwWhy - read by the parser, absent from the template, therefore never emitted. NULL IS NOT ZERO AT ALL THREE: sockets 0 is a MEASUREMENT that it has none, null is could-not-tell; eth False is visibly-not-ethereal, null is unknown. Sockets bounded 0..6 BY THE GAME so 7 is a misread not a rare item. VERIFIED LIVE: ethereal 4-socket gives sockets 4 eth True quality white; plain gives 0 False white; a silent reader gives None None None. ⚠ AND I CAUGHT A READER WITH NO WRITER BEFORE SHIPPING IT: the heart row counts sightings read by prompt X, and promptVer appeared ZERO times in vault_seen.json while the row carried only name lane kind witnesses conf lastSeenTs - so the watcher keyed on a field nothing wrote and would have read UNKNOWN forever while this version own note claimed a row records which prompt produced it. A claim in a ship note is not a join. promptVer is now stamped on the row and verified live as vp3368, and it is load-bearing: a null from vp2017 means the prompt never asked while a null from vp3368 means the reader could not tell, and without the stamp those are the same bytes.
